mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced consumer spending power, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and drives lower S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower (p > 0.05) when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses wage growth and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which correlates with lower earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower (p > 0.05) during periods of sustained INDPRO contraction relative to its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the housing starts index (HOUST) and personal savings rate (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month averages signals a shift from saving to spending, which boosts consumer demand and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the CPI inflation index (CPIAUCSL) below 1.5% while the federal funds rate remains above 2% indicates a disinflationary environment with restrictive policy, which tends to depress growth-sensitive equities and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 1.5% and FEDFUNDS > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when CPIAUCSL < 1.5% and FEDFUNDS > 2% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above the 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during four consecutive months of above-average PAYEMS growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months indicates reduced precautionary balances, which increases marginal propensity to consume and supports higher corporate revenues, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when RSAFS is below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months.
